title: Boss: The Wipe-Out
story: A sale just ended for 'Debugging the Monsoon' (id 3). The intern's query would zero the copies of EVERY book. Stop the disaster.
goal: Fix the query so only book id 3 gets copies = 0.
setup:
CREATE TABLE books (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, title TEXT NOT NULL, author TEXT, year INTEGER, price REAL, copies INTEGER DEFAULT 1);
INSERT INTO books VALUES (1,'Chilaka Learns Loops','Asha',2023,199.0,4),(2,'The Banyan Algorithm','Ravi',2021,349.0,2),(3,'Debugging the Monsoon','Meena',2024,275.0,6),(4,'Seeds of Python','Kiran',2022,150.0,10),(5,'Night Shift SRE','Lakshmi',2020,420.0,0);

hints: Run the starter on a copy of your thinking: which rows would it change? All of them.
Add a WHERE clause that matches only id 3.
UPDATE books SET copies = 0 WHERE id = 3;
socratic: Which rows does the starter touch?
How do you pick exactly one row?
Compare the rows you got with the rows expected. What differs?
explain: In one sentence: what was wrong with the query, and how did you fix it?
